method: Authenticator data is a byte string of at least 37 bytes. The first 32 bytes are the SHA-256 hash of the RP ID the credential is scoped to, the next byte is a flag field and the last four of the header are the signature counter as a 32-bit unsigned big-endian integer. In the flag byte bit 0 is User Present (0x01), bit 1 is reserved, bit 2 is User Verified (0x04), bit 3 is Backup Eligibility (0x08), bit 4 is Backup State (0x10), bit 5 is reserved, bit 6 marks attested credential data (0x40) and bit 7 marks extension data (0x80). When 0x40 is set, 16 bytes of AAGUID, a 2-byte big-endian credential ID length L that must be from 1 to 1,023, L bytes of credential ID and a COSE key follow; the page reads the CBOR item length so the key can be separated from what follows, then reads the integer parameters of the COSE key map: 1 is the key type, 3 the algorithm and -1 the curve, named from the COSE registries. When 0x80 is set a single CBOR map of extensions closes the structure; its encoded length and entry count are reported. Input is base64url with optional padding or hex with optional spaces, at most 12,288 characters and 4,096 decoded bytes. CBOR is read only in its definite-length form, to 16 levels and without indefinite-length items, and bytes left over after the structure the flags describe are refused rather than ignored. The page decodes bytes and reports what they say: it does not verify a signature, evaluate an attestation statement, compare the RP ID hash with a hostname or trust an AAGUID, so a valid parse is not proof that a registration or assertion is genuine. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads, accounts or network access.
